name: Amankora
positioning: Amankora, a Bhutan lodge circuit from Aman; the Paro lodge has an open-plan bedroom layout, a two-storey spa and views of Jhomolhari mountain
best_for: Travelers who want a base near the Tiger's Nest hike with a spa
Travelers who want to stay across several lodges in Bhutan

facts.text: Amankora is a circuit through Bhutan broken across five lodges among the Himalayas.
Amankora arrived in 2004 as the first international hospitality brand permitted to operate in Bhutan.
The Paro lodge opened first, with the full five-lodge circuit completed three years later.
The late Kerry Hill designed the lodges in the government-mandated style of whitewashed rammed-earth walls and wooden-framed windows.
The open-plan bedrooms at Amankora Paro have a king-size bed, a wood-burning stove and banquette window seating.
Amankora Paro has views of the snow-covered Jhomolhari mountain.
The Paro spa has two storeys, five treatment rooms, a hot stone bath, sauna, steam room and yoga studio.
At each lodge restaurant there is an a la carte of Western and fusion dishes plus a rotating set menu that alternates between Bhutanese and another Asian cuisine, Indian at Paro.
Most ingredients come from local farmers and the lodges' own kitchen gardens.
Tiger's Nest is a quick drive from the Paro lodge, as is the National Museum of Bhutan, housed inside a 17th-century watchtower.

highlights.text: After the hike to Tiger's Nest, guests can have a recovery lunch at Amankora's Log Cabin in the shadow of the monastery.
The Himalayan Hot Stone Bath uses heated river stones lowered into the bath, and local Khempa herbs infuse the water.
The Amankora Paro dining room has a terrace overlooking the 17th-century Drukgyel Dzong.
The late Kerry Hill designed the lodges in the government-mandated style of whitewashed rammed-earth walls and wooden-framed windows.

considerations.text: Travelers should expect long transfers to reach the lodges.
Any trip to Bhutan requires a licensed guide and driver, which Amankora can arrange but guests are not required to book through it.
There are no televisions in any room, nor a mini-bar.
